text:
Anthony Cirelli was a game-time call on Nov. 17 after missing two games, played, and added an empty-net goal against Washington. He is Tampa Bay's matchup center: 15 points in 20 games on 17 minutes a night, and steady value while the Kucherov trade talk takes up the oxygen.

The Lightning control 62.1% of the 5v5 expected goals with him on the ice, 6.8 points better than without him. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking found a signature last season: 20% of his setups come across the royal road (the pass across the slot that moves a goalie side to side), against 7% for a typical forward.

The numbers pull both ways. His teammates have been unlucky with him on the ice, 4.5 fewer goals than their chances deserve, which should swing back into assists. His own shooting runs the other way, 20% on just 30 shots. Evolving-Hockey notes he plays with very strong teammates (99th percentile), which flatters his on-ice numbers. Our range has him at 48 to 71 points.
